doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Why the sax player did not join the drum-solo fills; speed of thought
summary: Harris explains the music differs every night, jazz is a practice made on stage, and improvisation works at the speed of intuition.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah. I thought it was a marvelous — what I heard on the preview — a combination of something that was obviously arranged and written out, but then it veered off, came back, and what you’re talking about, the equal contribution of all the players was very evident. I wanted to ask, this could be like minutiae, but I’m fascinated about musical decisions and orchestrations. There’s a point, I believe it was in the first song which was fairly long. And there’s a drum solo. And everybody in the band except the sax player is going [scats] followed by Terreon filling in and then another [scats]. And it happened a number of times. So why didn’t the sax player go [scats]?

I mean it’s like one of those things that sometimes he’ll do it, sometimes he won’t. You never know. I mean the music is different every single time and it could have been a conscious decision on his part that he didn’t feel that that texture was necessary, or he may have been thinking about something else. That’s the interesting thing about this art form. It’s really — I’ve heard Marc Cary describe it as much more of a practice. It’s not so much that you are learning music in advance and then you’re executing. The actual beauty of the art form is the practice of making music on stage. So we are doing jazz when we’re there together so whatever level of engagement that you have is a manifestation of jazz. Whether it is to push forward with a strong idea to influence others, or to step back and give space for other people to shine. You know the other amazing thing about improvisation is the speed of thought. Things happen so quickly. It’s actually much more connected to intuition, which I think is just a really fast form of thinking. But © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

you can’t think through every step in advance. Because once the music goes this way it’s highly likely it’s not going to continue. You don’t know what it’s going to do. So if it pivots you have to constantly be listening and ready to go wherever the community, the team decides to go.
